note: Raw, unprocessed rover images. A geolocated photo is placed at the ROVER's NASA localization for the image's site/drive; the camera may be looking tens to hundreds of metres away. Rover camera heights (about 1-2 m) are not an astronaut's eye level.

selection.summary: Candidates are NASA raw images from the sealing sol and the three sols before it (seven when that gives fewer than six terrain photos; landing: sols 13-16). Near-duplicate frames are skipped. Each frame gets an AUTOMATIC category from NASA metadata (camera, pointing, frame size, image id) and simple statistics of NASA's 320 px browse image (contrast, texture, sky band, grey/smooth areas). Categories are heuristics and can be wrong; they are not NASA labels.

categories.landscape: A bright, smooth sky band at the top of the frame: the horizon is in view.
categories.geology: Mast camera aimed at terrain away from the rover without the horizon: outcrops, layered rocks, ridges.
categories.rocks: Mast camera aimed steeply down at the ground near the rover, or an arm/telescopic close-up (WATSON, SuperCam RMI).
categories.other: Kept aside: CacheCam sample tubes, Hazcam views (arm/wheels in frame), rover-frame pointings or Mastcam-Z sequences reused at 3+ stops (turret, drill bits, deck, calibration targets), grey/smooth hardware-like frames, sky-only, blank or dark frames.

places.at_site: The image's NASA site/drive localization is the same one the sample marker uses.
places.nearby: A different NASA localization within 150 m of the marker's localization.
places.regional: A different NASA localization 150-1500 m from the marker's localization.
places.not_geolocated: NASA has no (non-interpolated) localization for the image's site/drive; it is not placed on the map.
